newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down in correction.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down in correction.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed weaker but above lows in a technical correction to the recent climb to seven-month highs, trading sources said.
"The market had a good move up for a while but there was no follow-through or physical demand," a broker said.

Sell stops were triggered from the open, when the May contract traded below support pegged at 11.09 cents a lb, also the previous upside target. About 2,000 lots were sold on stops once July reached 10.89 cents, the broker said.
Steady trade buying held May around support at 11.10 cents, but persistent selling knocked the spot month to its low of 10.87 cents.
Trade buying lifted prices off the lows on the close.
Fundamentally, the ample supplies that have come to the market recently added fundamental pressure to prices, Refco analyst Anne Prendergast, said.
"The market ran up because everyone thught there wouldn't be enough sugar for May delivery," she said, referring to May's climb to 11.38 cents on April 10.
"But high prices attracted producers to release sugar, and that took us back down again," Prendergast said.
Nearby support was seen between 10.90 and 10.80 cents in May, and then at 10.75.
May settled 0.18 cent lower at 10.95 cents, traded from 11.10 to 10.87. Most-active July fell 0.16 cent to 10.85, while the remaining months finished 0.11 to 0.05 weaker.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 44,599 lots.
The last trading day for the May contract is April 30.
Open interest in May fell 1,467 lots to 55,622 lots as of Monday's close, while open interest in July climbed 4,608 lots to 64,546 lots.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640))
